title: An August
logline: Small Wood in vol 7's summer, in the background of a private page: a girl at a coffee counter, zines in a bookstore window, a crow, the ridge glow at its largest, the eye sign.

panels.composition: Main street, August, from the seawall end, looking up the hill. In the foreground, WOOD from behind with BARNABY II. Up the street, small, none of it foregrounded: a coffee place with a girl at the counter in an apron, something dark on her thigh the drawing doesn't resolve; a bookstore window with photocopied zines fanned in it; a crow on a railing; a yellow square sign with a single eye on a pole; a fish weathervane above it. On the ridge east of town, the glow, larger than any Sunday ever drew it, in daylight.
props: a girl at a coffee counter, small

image.prompt: a small coastal main street in August seen from its seawall end looking uphill, a man from behind with a three-legged dog in the foreground, and small in the background a coffee counter with a girl in an apron, a bookstore window fanned with photocopied zines, a crow on a railing, a yellow square street sign bearing a single eye on a pole with a fish weathervane above it, and on the forested ridge beyond the town a pale glow visible even in daylight, spare ink with muted ochre and sea-foam watercolor, no panel borders, no words
image.notes: Vol 7's August, unnamed: Lena at the Daily Grind, Static Truths in the Salty Tome's window, the crow, the tower's glow. Nothing foregrounded. Felt, not adhered to.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: The echo page. The saga's other volume walks through the background.
